items.label: LEMMA
items.mechanism: Queue stores jobs in a deque; push() appends and pop() takes from the left

items.label: LEMMA
items.statement: Automatic retries with exponential backoff for failing jobs.
items.mechanism: run_with_retry() re-runs a failing callable up to `attempts` times, sleeping base_delay * 2 ** attempt between tries
items.gap: Backoff itself is tested, but retry is a standalone helper: Queue never calls run_with_retry(), so a job popped from the queue is only retried if the caller wraps it by hand. No test covers a queued job being retried.

items.label: LEMMA
items.mechanism: push() returns False without enqueuing when the job id is already in the pending-id set
items.gap: Only jobs still pending are deduplicated: pop() discards the id, so the same id is accepted again afterwards. The test checks push()'s return value but not that the queue holds a single item, and nothing tests re-push after pop.

items.label: LEMMA
items.statement: Jobs are persisted to disk and survive restarts.
items.gap: Queue is in-memory only (a deque and a set); no file, database or serialisation code exists, and no test restarts a queue and reads jobs back.

items.label: LEMMA
items.statement: Thread-safe: share one queue across worker threads.
items.gap: No lock or thread-safe structure guards Queue; push() does an unguarded check-then-add on _ids, so two threads can enqueue the same id, and pop() on an empty queue raises IndexError instead of blocking. No concurrency test.
